import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Crouzeix's conjecture

Crouzeix's conjecture (2004) states that for every square complex matrix $A$ and every
complex function $f$ that is analytic in the interior of the field of values $W(A)$ of $A$ and
continuous up to the boundary of $W(A)$,
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm. Equivalently, the inequality holds for
every complex polynomial $p$ in place of $f$.

Two independent proofs of the conjecture were announced in 2026 (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger
[LS26]). As of August 2026 these are recent preprints that have not yet appeared in a
peer-reviewed venue, so the conjecture is recorded here as open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crouzeix%27s_conjecture)
- [Cr04] Crouzeix, M. "Bounds for Analytical Functions of Matrices." Integral Equations and
  Operator Theory 48 (2004), 461–477. [doi](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6)
- [CP17] Crouzeix, M., Palencia, C. "The Numerical Range is a $(1+\sqrt2)$-Spectral Set." SIAM
  Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications 38 (2017), 649–655.
  [doi](https://doi.org/10.1137/17M1116672)
- [LS26] Lorist, E., Schwenninger, F. "A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture."
  [arXiv:2608.03841](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.03841)
-/

open Polynomial Filter Topology
open scoped InnerProductSpace Matrix.Norms.L2Operator

namespace CrouzeixsConjecture

variable {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- The **field of values** (or **numerical range**) of a square complex matrix `A`:
$$W(A) = \{\langle Ax, x\rangle : x \in \mathbb{C}^n, \|x\| = 1\}
  = \{x^* A x : x \in \mathbb{C}^n, \|x\| = 1\}.$$
Here `⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ` is Mathlib's inner product on `EuclideanSpace ℂ n`. It is conjugate-linear in
its first argument, so `⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ = ∑ i, conj (x i) * (A x) i = x^* A x`. -/
def numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ ⟪x, Matrix.toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ = z}

/-- The field of values of a matrix is a compact subset of `ℂ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
theorem isCompact_numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : IsCompact (numericalRange A) := by
  have : numericalRange A =
      (fun x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n => ⟪x, Matrix.toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ) ''
        Metric.sphere 0 1 := by
    ext z
    simp [numericalRange]
  rw [this]
  exact (isCompact_sphere 0 1).image
    (continuous_id.inner (LinearMap.continuous_of_finiteDimensional _))

@[category test, AMS 15]
theorem numericalRange_one [Nonempty n] : numericalRange (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) = {1} := by
  have h1 : ∀ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, Matrix.toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix n n ℂ) x = x := by
    intro x
    simp [Matrix.toEuclideanLin_apply]
  ext z
  simp only [numericalRange, Set.mem_setOf_eq, Set.mem_singleton_iff, h1,
    inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    simp [hx]
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨EuclideanSpace.single (Classical.arbitrary n) 1, by simp, by simp⟩

/--
**Crouzeix's conjecture** (polynomial form). For every $n \geq 1$, every $n \times n$ complex
matrix $A$ and every complex polynomial $p$,
$$\|p(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|,$$
where $W(A)$ is the field of values of $A$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.polynomial [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖p.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
**Crouzeix's conjecture**. Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ complex matrix, $n \geq 1$, and let $f$ be a
complex function that is analytic in the interior of the field of values $W(A)$ and continuous
up to the boundary of $W(A)$. Then
$$\|f(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm.

Here $f(A)$ is the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus $p \mapsto p(A)$:
$f(A)$ is the limit of $p_k(A)$ for any sequence of polynomials $p_k$ converging to $f$ uniformly
on $W(A)$. The statement quantifies over the matrix `fA` obtained in this way.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A))
    (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)))
    (fA : Matrix n n ℂ) (p : ℕ → ℂ[X])
    (hp : TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z => (p k).eval z) f atTop (numericalRange A))
    (hpA : Tendsto (fun k => aeval A (p k)) atTop (𝓝 fA)) :
    ‖fA‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖ := by
  sorry

/-- Crouzeix's conjecture holds for normal matrices. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.normal [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ) [IsStarNormal A]
    (p : ℂ[X]) :
    ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖p.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
**Crouzeix–Palencia theorem** [CP17]. For every square complex matrix $A$ and every complex
polynomial $p$,
$$\|p(A)\| \leq (1 + \sqrt 2) \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|.$$
This improves Crouzeix's 2007 bound with the constant $11.08$. Crouzeix's conjecture asserts that
the constant can be lowered to $2$. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.crouzeix_palencia [Nonempty n] (A : Matrix n n ℂ)
    (p : ℂ[X]) :
    ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ (1 + √2) * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖p.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

end CrouzeixsConjecture

modeling_decisions: Norm: `open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` makes ‖·‖ on `Matrix n n ℂ` the operator norm induced by the Euclidean norm (spectral 2-norm), as required by the article; checked with `example : ‖aeval A p‖ = ‖Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (aeval A p)‖ := rfl`.

Field of values: defined as {⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ : x ∈ EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1} using `Matrix.toEuclideanLin`. Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the FIRST argument, so ⟪x, A x⟫ = ∑ conj(x_i)(Ax)_i = x^* A x, which is the standard ⟨Ax, x⟩ of the literature (checked: it equals `star x ⬝ᵥ (A *ᵥ x)` by rfl after `inner_eq_star_dotProduct`). Using ⟪A x, x⟫ in Mathlib's convention would have given the complex conjugate set, which changes sup|p| and would be wrong.

Supremum: `⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖` in ℝ. W(A) is compact (proved as API lemma `isCompact_numericalRange`) and nonempty (we assume `[Nonempty n]`), and f (resp. p) is continuous on it, so the set of values is nonempty and bounded above and the iSup is the genuine supremum; the `sSup ∅ = 0` junk for z ∉ W(A) is harmless since all values are ≥ 0.

Dimension: `[Nonempty n]` encodes n ≥ 1 (an n×n matrix with n ≥ 1, as in the notes). For n = 0 the statement would be the trivial 0 ≤ 0, so this only excludes a degenerate case; it also guarantees W(A) ≠ ∅ so the supremum is not a junk value.

f(A) in the analytic slot: Mathlib has no holomorphic/Riesz–Dunford functional calculus for non-normal matrices and no functional calculus for A(W(A)). Following the notes (f(A) is the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus), the statement quantifies over a matrix `fA` together with a sequence of polynomials p_k → f uniformly on W(A) (`TendstoUniformlyOn`) with p_k(A) → fA. Such sequences exist for every f ∈ A(W(A)) by Mergelyan's theorem (W(A) is compact convex, so its complement is connected), and the limit exists and is unique by Crouzeix's/Crouzeix–Palencia's proven bound, so `fA` is exactly f(A) and the statement is equivalent to ‖f(A)‖ ≤ 2 sup_{W(A)} |f|. No junk-valued `limUnder` definition was introduced.

Analyticity: encoded as `DifferentiableOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A))`, equivalent to analyticity because the interior is open; when the interior is empty (e.g. normal A with collinear spectrum) the hypothesis is vacuous, matching the source. Continuity up to the boundary is `ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A)` (W(A) is closed, so W(A) is its own closure). These two hypotheses are logically redundant given the uniform-approximation hypothesis, but are kept so the statement reads as in the source.

These use the same polynomial formulation.

Category kept `research open` per the task status; the module docstring records the 2026 announced proofs (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger) as recent preprints, following the precedent of other files in the repo.

namespace CrouzeixsConjecture

open Set
open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator

/-- The numerical range (field of values) of a complex square matrix `A`. Thus
`numericalRange A` consists of the scalars $x^* A x$ for unit vectors $x$. -/
def numericalRange {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧
    inner ℂ x (Matrix.toEuclideanCLM (n := n) (𝕜 := ℂ) A x) = z}

/-- `IsMatrixFunctionalCalculus A f B` says that `B` is the value $f(A)$ obtained by
continuously extending polynomial evaluation: a polynomial can simultaneously approximate
$f$ uniformly on the numerical range of `A` and its value at `A` arbitrarily closely to `B`. -/
def IsMatrixFunctionalCalculus {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∃ p : Polynomial ℂ,
    ‖Polynomial.aeval A p - B‖ < ε ∧
      ∀ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖Polynomial.eval z p - f z‖ < ε

/-- **Crouzeix's conjecture.** For every positive dimension, complex square matrix $A$, and
complex function $f$ continuous on $W(A)$ and analytic on its interior, the continuous extension
$f(A)$ of polynomial matrix evaluation satisfies
$$\lVert f(A)\rVert_2 \leq 2\sup_{z\in W(A)} |f(z)|.$$
Here $W(A)$ is the numerical range and the matrix norm is the spectral operator $2$-norm. -/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ),
      ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A) →
      AnalyticOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)) →
      ∃ B : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ, IsMatrixFunctionalCalculus A f B ∧
        ‖B‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖f z‖) '' numericalRange A) := by
  sorry

/-- **Polynomial form of Crouzeix's conjecture.** For every positive dimension, complex square
matrix $A$, and complex polynomial $p$,
$$\lVert p(A)\rVert_2 \leq 2\sup_{z\in W(A)} |p(z)|,$$
where `Polynomial.aeval A p` is $p(A)$, $W(A)$ is the numerical range, and the matrix norm is the
spectral operator $2$-norm. -/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.polynomial :
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 0 < n → ∀ (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (p : Polynomial ℂ),
      ‖Polynomial.aeval A p‖ ≤
        2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖Polynomial.eval z p‖) '' numericalRange A) := by
  sorry

end CrouzeixsConjecture
modeling_decisions: Represented every positive matrix dimension by `n : ℕ` together with `0 < n`, and matrices by `Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ`.
Defined the numerical range as the set of `inner ℂ x (A x) = x* A x` over Euclidean unit vectors. This fixes the inner-product convention to the standard field-of-values scalar.
Used Mathlib's scoped `Matrix.Norms.L2Operator` norm, whose definition is induced by `Matrix.toEuclideanCLM`, for the spectral operator 2-norm.

Represented the Delyon–Delyon/Crouzeix extension by the closure of the graph of polynomial evaluation: a matrix `B` is `f(A)` when, for every positive epsilon, one polynomial uniformly approximates `f` on `W(A)` while its evaluation at `A` approximates `B` in operator norm. The main statement explicitly existentially supplies such a `B`, avoiding vacuity from an unformalized existence theorem.
Formalized continuity as `ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A)` and analyticity as `AnalyticOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A))`; the latter is vacuous when the interior is empty, as required.

Used real `sSup` of the image of the pointwise complex norm over the numerical range. For every stated dimension the numerical range is nonempty and compact, so this denotes the intended finite supremum.
Used `Polynomial.aeval A p` for polynomial matrix evaluation and `Polynomial.eval z p` for scalar evaluation.

The numerical range (or field of values) of a complex matrix $A$ is
$W(A) = \{x^* A x : \lVert x\rVert_2 = 1\}$.
-/
noncomputable def numericalRange {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : Set ℂ :=
  {z | ∃ x : EuclideanSpace ℂ n, ‖x‖ = 1 ∧ z = inner ℂ x (A.toEuclideanLin x)}

/--
`IsMatrixFunction A f B` means that $B$ is $f(A)$ under the continuous extension of the
polynomial functional calculus: some sequence of polynomials converges uniformly to $f$ on
$W(A)$, while its evaluations at $A$ converge to $B$.
-/
noncomputable def IsMatrixFunction {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (B : Matrix n n ℂ) : Prop :=
  ∃ p : ℕ → ℂ[X],
    TendstoUniformlyOn (fun k z ↦ (p k).eval z) f atTop (numericalRange A) ∧
      Tendsto (fun k ↦ Polynomial.aeval A (p k)) atTop (𝓝 B)

/--
**Crouzeix's conjecture.** For every nonempty finite square complex matrix $A$ and every
complex function $f$ that is continuous on $W(A)$ and analytic on its interior, the continuous
polynomial-functional-calculus value $f(A)$ exists and satisfies
$\lVert f(A)\rVert_2 \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|$, where the matrix norm is the spectral
operator $2$-norm.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture
    {n : Type*} [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n] [Nonempty n]
    (A : Matrix n n ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ)

    (hf_analytic : AnalyticOnNhd ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A))) :
    ∃ B : Matrix n n ℂ, IsMatrixFunction A f B ∧
      ‖B‖ ≤ 2 * sSup {r : ℝ | ∃ z ∈ numericalRange A, r = ‖f z‖} := by
  sorry

**Polynomial form of Crouzeix's conjecture.** For every nonempty finite square complex matrix
$A$ and every complex polynomial $p$,
$\lVert p(A)\rVert_2 \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|$, where $p(A)$ is
`Polynomial.aeval A p` and the matrix norm is the spectral operator $2$-norm.
-/

theorem isCompact_numericalRange (A : Matrix n n ℂ) : IsCompact (numericalRange A) :=

    (B : Matrix n n ℂ) (hB : IsFunCalc A f B) :
    ‖B‖ ≤ 2 * sSup ((fun z => ‖f z‖) '' numericalRange A) := by

$$\|p(A)\| \leq 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|,$$

/-- The numerical range of the identity matrix is `{1}` (in positive dimension). -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
lemma numericalRange_one : numericalRange (1 : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℂ) = {1} := by
  have h : toEuclideanLin (1 : Matrix (Fin (n + 1)) (Fin (n + 1)) ℂ) = LinearMap.id :=
    LinearMap.ext fun v => by simp [toEuclideanLin_apply]
  ext w
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, hx]
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 1, by simp, by simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]⟩

/-- The numerical range of the `1 × 1` matrix `(a)` is `{a}` (and not `{conj a}`). -/
@[category test, AMS 15]
lemma numericalRange_fin_one (a : ℂ) : numericalRange !![a] = {a} := by
  have h : toEuclideanLin !![a] = a • LinearMap.id :=
    LinearMap.ext fun v => by ext i; fin_cases i; simp [toEuclideanLin_apply, vecHead]
  ext w
  constructor
  · rintro ⟨x, hx, rfl⟩
    simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, hx]
  · rintro rfl
    exact ⟨EuclideanSpace.single 0 1, by simp, by simp [h, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K]⟩

/-- Every eigenvalue of a square complex matrix lies in its numerical range. -/
@[category API, AMS 15]
lemma spectrum_subset_numericalRange (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) :
    spectrum ℂ A ⊆ numericalRange A := by
  intro μ hμ
  rw [← spectrum_toLin A (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℂ).toBasis,
    ← Module.End.hasEigenvalue_iff_mem_spectrum] at hμ
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hμ.exists_hasEigenvector
  have hx0 : ‖x‖ ≠ 0 := norm_ne_zero_iff.mpr hx.2
  refine ⟨(‖x‖⁻¹ : ℂ) • x, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [norm_smul, hx0]
  · rw [toEuclideanLin_eq_toLin_orthonormal, map_smul, hx.apply_eq_smul, smul_comm,
      inner_smul_right, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right, inner_self_eq_norm_sq_to_K, map_inv₀,
      Complex.conj_ofReal]
    have : (‖x‖ : ℂ) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hx0
    field_simp
    simp only [RCLike.ofReal_eq_complex_ofReal]

/-- A family of polynomials converges along `uniformApproxFilter s f` iff it converges uniformly
to `f` on `s`. -/
@[category API, AMS 41]
lemma tendsto_uniformApproxFilter_iff {ι : Type*} {l : Filter ι} {P : ι → ℂ[X]} {s : Set ℂ}
    {f : ℂ → ℂ} :
    Tendsto P l (uniformApproxFilter s f) ↔
      TendstoUniformlyOn (fun i z => (P i).eval z) f l s := by
  simp only [uniformApproxFilter, tendsto_iInf, tendsto_principal, Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff,
    dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_rev, Set.mem_setOf_eq]

/-- **Crouzeix's conjecture.** Let $A$ be an $n \times n$ complex matrix with field of values
$W(A)$, and let $f$ be a complex function that is analytic in the interior of $W(A)$ and
continuous up to the boundary of $W(A)$. Then
$$\|f(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |f(z)|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm and $f(A)$ is given by the continuous
extension of the polynomial functional calculus (see `analyticCalculus`). -/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hf : ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A))
    (hf' : DifferentiableOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A))) :
    ‖analyticCalculus A f‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖ := by
  sorry

/-- **Crouzeix's conjecture**, polynomial form. For every $n \times n$ complex matrix $A$ and every
complex polynomial $p$,
$$\|p(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z \in W(A)} |p(z)|,$$
where $W(A)$ is the field of values of $A$ and $\|\cdot\|$ is the spectral operator $2$-norm. -/
@[category research open, AMS 15 47]
theorem crouzeixs_conjecture.variants.polynomial (A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ) (p : ℂ[X]) :
    ‖aeval A p‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖p.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

end CrouzeixsConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The two slots (analytic form and polynomial form) match the Wikipedia article exactly. The only remark: the table's note that the polynomial form is 'equivalent to the analytic form by density of polynomials' is correct but the equivalence itself relies on Mergelyan's theorem and on the (proved) Crouzeix 2007 bound to make f(A) well defined; the analytic slot as stated in the file inherits this dependence through the definition of analyticCalculus.
modeling_decisions: Matrices are indexed by Fin n with n : ℕ arbitrary (including n = 0). For n = 0 both sides are 0 (W(A) = ∅, ⨆ over ∅ in ℝ is 0, the unique 0×0 matrix has norm 0), so the statement is trivially true there and no `0 < n` hypothesis was added; the notes' 'n ≥ 1' is therefore not a restriction that changes the claim.

The spectral operator 2-norm is obtained via `open scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator`, making ‖·‖ on Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ the instance Matrix.instL2OpNormedRing; checked with #synth and Matrix.cstar_norm_def that ‖A‖ = ‖toEuclideanCLM A‖ (operator norm on EuclideanSpace).

Numerical range uses ⟪x, A x⟫_ℂ (Mathlib inner product, conjugate-linear in the first argument) = x*Ax. The Wikipedia/list notation ⟨Ax, x⟩ with the mathematicians' convention (linear in the first argument) denotes the same number. Using ⟪A x, x⟫_ℂ in Mathlib would give the complex-conjugate set, which is wrong.

The supremum sup_{z ∈ W(A)} |f(z)| is written `⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖` in ℝ. Since W(A) is compact and f is continuous on it, this is the genuine supremum (bounded, nonempty for n ≥ 1); Real.iSup's junk value 0 for empty/unbounded index only occurs at n = 0 where the inequality is 0 ≤ 0.

'Analytic in the interior of W(A) and continuous up to the boundary' is formalized as `DifferentiableOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A))` (complex differentiability on an open set = analyticity) together with `ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A)` (W(A) is closed for matrices). f : ℂ → ℂ is a total function; its values outside W(A) do not affect either side of the inequality (the filter and the sup only see f on W(A)). When interior W(A) = ∅ (e.g. normal A with collinear spectrum) the analyticity hypothesis is vacuous, as in the informal statement.

f(A) is formalized as `limUnder` along the uniform-approximation filter. This matches the literature's definition (continuous extension of p ↦ p(A) to A(W(A))). A reviewer should note that its correctness as 'the' f(A) relies on two proved theorems (Mergelyan's theorem for density of polynomials on the compact convex set W(A), and Crouzeix's 2007 theorem for continuity of p ↦ p(A)); if either failed, limUnder would return a junk value. Both theorems hold, so the Lean statement is exactly the conjecture. An alternative formulation (∀ B, (∃ polynomial sequence p_k → f uniformly on W(A) with p_k(A) → B) → ‖B‖ ≤ 2 sup |f|) was considered and rejected as less direct, though it is equivalent given the same theorems.

The topology used by limUnder is the Pi topology on matrices (instTopologicalSpaceMatrix), which coincides with the L2 operator-norm topology (finite dimension; Mathlib builds the L2 instance with replaceTopology to agree with it).

Both slots are tagged `research open` per the given status, even though the article reports proofs announced in 2026 (Jin; Lorist–Schwenninger); these are mentioned as announced in the module docstring with references.
The polynomial slot uses Polynomial.aeval A p for p(A) and p.eval z for p(z), as the notes prescribe.

Bespoke definitions are placed in the problem file (inside namespace CrouzeixsConjecture) because only the single candidate file may be written; numericalRange and uniformApproxFilter are generic enough that a maintainer might prefer to move them to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

new_definitions.name: CrouzeixsConjecture.numericalRange
new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no definition of the numerical range / field of values W(A) = {⟨x, Ax⟩ : ‖x‖ = 1}. Defined for A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ as the set of ⟪x, toEuclideanLin A x⟫_ℂ over unit vectors x of EuclideanSpace ℂ (Fin n) (Euclidean norm, not the sup norm of Fin n → ℂ). Mathlib's inner product is conjugate-linear in the first argument, so this is x*Ax, the standard convention; ⟪A x, x⟫ would give the conjugate set. Validated by API lemmas numericalRange_one, numericalRange_fin_one (W(!![a]) = {a}) and spectrum_subset_numericalRange.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: Filter.comap of the neighbourhood filter in UniformFun/UniformOnFun; TendstoUniformlyOn (a predicate on families, not a filter on polynomials). The explicit ⨅ ε > 0, 𝓟 {...} form was chosen for readability and is proved equivalent to TendstoUniformlyOn.
new_definitions.name: CrouzeixsConjecture.uniformApproxFilter
new_definitions.why_needed: The filter on ℂ[X] generated by the sets {p | ∀ z ∈ s, ‖p.eval z - f z‖ < ε} for ε > 0, i.e. 'p → f uniformly on s'. Needed to express the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus. API lemma tendsto_uniformApproxFilter_iff shows Tendsto P l (uniformApproxFilter s f) ↔ TendstoUniformlyOn (fun i z => (P i).eval z) f l s.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: cfc / cfcₙ (only for normal elements, not general matrices); Polynomial.aeval (polynomials only, used as the base of the extension); NormedSpace.exp (a single function). None cover general f ∈ A(W(A)) for non-normal A.
new_definitions.name: CrouzeixsConjecture.analyticCalculus
new_definitions.why_needed: f(A) for f continuous on W(A) and analytic in its interior. Mathlib has no holomorphic (Riesz–Dunford) functional calculus and its continuous functional calculus applies only to normal elements. In the literature (Delyon–Delyon 1999, Crouzeix 2007, Malman–Mashreghi–O'Loughlin–Ransford) f(A) is defined as the continuous extension of p ↦ p(A) from polynomials to A(W(A)). Defined as limUnder (uniformApproxFilter (numericalRange A) f) (fun p => aeval A p). The limit exists and is unique by two established theorems: Mergelyan (polynomials are dense in A(W(A)) since W(A) is compact convex, so the filter is NeBot) and Crouzeix 2007 (‖p(A)‖ ≤ 11.08 sup_{W(A)} |p|, so p ↦ p(A) is uniformly continuous in the sup norm on W(A)).

crouzeixs_conjecture.why: Stated as: for all n, all A : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) ℂ and all f : ℂ → ℂ with ContinuousOn f (numericalRange A) and DifferentiableOn ℂ f (interior (numericalRange A)), ‖analyticCalculus A f‖ ≤ 2 * ⨆ z ∈ numericalRange A, ‖f z‖, with ‖·‖ the L2 operator (spectral) norm via the scoped Matrix.Norms.L2Operator instance. Needed bespoke definitions of the numerical range and of f(A) as the continuous extension of the polynomial functional calculus (a limit along the filter of polynomials converging uniformly to f on W(A)).
